summary.title: Emerging Architectures for Modern Data Infrastructure
summary.one_liner: Learn the current reference architectures for analytic and operational data stacks, what changed since 2020, and the "data platform" hypothesis explaining why new tools keep appearing.
takeaways: The core data stack (ingestion, warehouse/lakehouse, transformation) has stayed relatively stable, while supporting tools and apps have proliferated.
Three blueprints are covered: Modern Business Intelligence, Multimodal Data Processing (lakehouse), and AI/ML infrastructure, each with a list of what changed.
A metrics layer, reverse ETL, data observability, and data workspaces are highlighted as newer categories.
The 'data platform hypothesis' argues that backend data systems are consolidating around a few cloud vendors, enabling many third-party data applications on top.
summary.summary: This is a 2021-era update from Andreessen Horowitz to its 2020 data infrastructure reference architectures, compiled from interviews with dozens of data practitioners. It diagrams an overall stack plus a machine learning chain, then walks through three blueprints (Modern Business Intelligence, Multimodal Data Processing, and AI/ML) listing what stayed the same and what changed. The final sections argue that data infrastructure is consolidating into "platforms" with mutual dependence between core vendors and third-party app developers, and close with a list of contributors.
